column1: # T-181 wave plan — WHICH slices run together, and in what order.
# Read by scripts/mod/wave.sh. This is DATA, not memory: any session (or a fresh one after a
# context reset) can run `bash scripts/mod/wave.sh status` and know exactly where the program is.
# Waves are batched by FILE DISJOINTNESS, not by count — see docs/mod/SLICE_WORKFLOW.md rule 6.
# TBD_SpawnManager.c and TBD_FrameworkManager.c are the contended files; two slices in the SAME
# wave must never both write one of them. `owns` records the write claim so conflicts are visible
# before dispatch rather than at merge.
# Max 3 slices per wave (disk: one worktree each).
